patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Genesys and Nextiva share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Genesys and Nextiva share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Genesys only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; ” rather than Nextiva's shape. Choose Nextiva only if your buying job matches “SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo” rather than Genesys's shape. Workflow advantage: Genesys leans sales-calling; Nextiva leans business-phone, team-communication. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Genesys and Nextiva share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Genesys is Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; CX 4 $240.; Nextiva is SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month annual, with messaging apps including WhatsApp.
- Company-size focus: Genesys (mid-market, enterprise) vs Nextiva (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Genesys-leaning sales-calling vs Nextiva-leaning business-phone, team-communication.
- Researched limits: Genesys — Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; Nextiva — Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included.

Limitations — Genesys: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; CX 1 is voice-only; digital channels require CX 2 or digital add-ons; Nextiva: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Analytics and AI assistance require Scale / higher plans or XBert add-on from $99/mo.

Poor-fit cases: Genesys is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone · Nextiva is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included · Avoid Genesys if you actually need Nextiva's motion (SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 p)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
